title: Annotated sequence clusters and pin recommendations for KV cache on long-context models
creator: Priya Raman
description: Goal: produce per-model, per-sequence-distribution KV cache performance artifacts plus deterministic version-pinning recommendations to be published to the profile registry. Focus model: llama3-70b-chat (open variant) and a customer-supplied fine-tuned variant. Deliverables: 1) annotated sequence clusters and signatures, 2) KV retention/eviction policy mapping by cluster, 3) pinned model-version recommendations and automated publish workflow for profiles, 4) benchmark dashboard and perf-cost trade-off analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Sequence clusters (>=3 clusters per model) with representative signatures and percentile latency/cost metrics published to profile registry
Pinning recommendations (model-version -> cluster) documented and implementable via rollout config
Automated CI job that validates profile vs. 95th percentile latency SLO on a canonical long-context harness
Confluence runbook and a dashboard link with stable visualizations for customer-facing teams
background: We observed regressions in latency and tail behavior for long-context chat sessions with llama3-70b-chat after model variant upgrades. Existing KV profiles are too coarse (single-profile-per-model) and do not capture sequence distribution skew (e.g., many short queries with intermittent >16k token sessions). This ticket evaluates a cluster-based profiling approach to better match cache retention and version pinning to real workload shapes.
work_summary: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and platform PMs. Agreed scope and models to onboard (llama3-70b-chat, customer-finetune-A). Action: produce 48-hour sample of production-like sequences from traffic proxy (anonymized).

2026-02-22: Data collection complete (2.1M sequences). Applied privacy-preserving bucketing and token-length histogram. Stored artifacts at gs://redwood-dev-profiles/eng/ENG-40212/raw_samples-v1 (link in comments).

2026-02-26: Implemented sequence fingerprinting: rolling hashed n-gram signature with temporal decay; created initial 5 cluster candidates using HDBSCAN on normalized features (seq_len, prefix_entropy, kv-hit-rate-estimate).

2026-03-01: Ran controlled perf sweep on dedicated infra (pools dcv2-large) across model versions v1.1, v1.2, v1.2-quant. Observed that cluster C_highlong (top 3% by length) shows 2.4x increased tail latency when pinned to v1.2-quant compared to v1.2. Baseline metrics published to perf dashboard (grafana link).

2026-03-05: Trade-off analysis meeting: accuracy vs cost for quantized pin. Decided to recommend hybrid pinning (v1.2 for clusters with >90th percentile lengths, v1.2-quant for short clusters) + KV retention extension for streaming sessions.
2026-03-09: Prototype publish pipeline added: profile artifact schema (profile_v2) and CI validator. Created PR #8692 (github.com/redwood/realtime/pulls/8692) with ingestion consumer and unit tests.
2026-03-12: PM review feedback received — asked to add a canary rollout step and an automated rollback threshold if 95th percentile latency increases by >15% vs baseline.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Clustered profiling chosen over per-sequence retention rules because clusters generalize across models and reduce profile churn.
Sampling frequency: 48-hour rolling windows strike balance between recency and noise; more frequent (hourly) profiles were noisy and caused thrashing of pin recommendations.
Pin policy: default to conservative (non-quantized) for long-seq clusters to avoid tail latency regressions; accept higher unit-cost for top-percentile sessions to maintain SLOs.

Privacy: sequences are hashed and histograms aggregated; raw text is not stored in profile artifacts. This increases uncertainty in content-sensitive heuristics (e.g., prefix entropy) so we bias towards longer retention when signal is ambiguous.
risks_and_blockers: Blocking: infra needs a rate-limited ingestion endpoint for profile registry (ticket INF-7845) before we can lock down automated publication cadence.
Risk: sampling bias from Canary traffic may underrepresent rare but expensive session patterns; we will mitigate by cross-checking with synthetic long-session workload runs.
Dependency: rollout automation in console requires small UI change (PM-581) to surface cluster-level pin overrides for customers on Dedicated plans.

implementation_notes: Profile_v2 schema fields: model_id, cluster_id, signature_hashes[], percentile_latencies (p50/p90/p95), kv_hit_rate_est, recommended_version, retention_ms, publish_timestamp, provenance (sampling_window_id).
CI validator: compares new profile percentiles against baseline profile for same model+cluster; fails if p95 increases >15% or p99 >20%.
Rollout plan: staged canary (1%), regional ramp (10%->50%->100%) with metrics gating; rollback on latency SLO breach or error-rate uptick.
Mapping heuristic: clusters with median_seq_len > 4096 => recommend non-quantized pinned version; median_seq_len between 512-4096 => recommend quantized-from-v1.2 if accuracy delta < 1% on eval set.
